specs.name: current_time
specs.description:
Get the current date and time in a timezone. Use this whenever the answer
depends on today's date or the time of day.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, for example America/Toronto or Asia/Kolkata.
timezone.title: Timezone

specs.name: update_plan
specs.description:
Show the user a checklist of the steps you are taking. Use it for tasks
that need three or more steps: call it before starting with the whole plan,
then again with the full updated list whenever a step's status changes.
Keep at most one step in_progress. Skip it for simple questions.

specs.name: web_search
specs.description:
Search the web. Returns titles, URLs and short snippets. Snippets are often
incomplete: use web_fetch on the most relevant URLs before relying on them.

topic.description: Use news for recent events and announcements.
topic.title: Topic

time_range.description: Only return pages published within this period.
time_range.title: Time Range

specs.name: web_fetch
specs.description:
Read a web page and return its main text as Markdown, with links. Use it
to read pages found with web_search or given by the user.

url.description: The full http(s) URL of the page to read.
url.title: Url

specs.name: record_observation
specs.description:
Record what a scheduled watch observed. Only use this when a scheduled
watch run asks you to. Call it once, with found=false if the target or value
could not be found.

input_schema.description: What a watch run saw. ``value`` is set when the extract is a number.
input_schema.title: Observation

specs.name: schedule_create
specs.description:
Propose a scheduled task or watch for the user to confirm.

Use kind=task with a prompt for recurring or one-time work ("every weekday at
8am summarize ..."), and kind=watch with a watch spec to monitor a value and
alert on a condition ("tell me when the fare drops under $1500"). Resolve
relative times ("tomorrow 8am") with current_time first, and give one-shot
times as ISO 8601 with an offset. The job stays inactive until the user
confirms it in the UI; tell the user what you proposed and the next run times
this tool returns.

Changed.description: The value moved by at least ``min_delta`` since the previous observation.
Changed.title: Changed

CronSchedule.description: Standard five-field cron, evaluated in local wall-clock time of ``timezone``.
CronSchedule.title: CronSchedule

IntervalSchedule.description: Every N seconds of elapsed time (daylight saving does not affect it).
IntervalSchedule.title: IntervalSchedule

WatchSpec.description: What to look at, what to extract, and when to raise an alert.

target.description: A URL, or a search query, describing where to look.
target.title: Target

extract.description: What to read from the target, e.g. 'lowest round-trip fare in CAD'.
extract.title: Extract

WatchSpec.title: WatchSpec

input_schema.description: The editable part of a job.

prompt.description: For tasks: what the agent should do.
prompt.title: Prompt

input_schema.title: JobSpec

specs.name: schedule_list
specs.description: List the user's scheduled tasks and watches with their status and next run.

specs.name: schedule_set_status
specs.description: Pause, resume or delete a scheduled job by id (see schedule_list).

status.description: active resumes a paused job; it cannot activate an unconfirmed one.
status.title: Status

specs.name: notify_me
specs.description:
Send the user a message by email and browser push, for example a summary
they asked to receive. It only reaches the user themselves and needs their
approval each time.

# Weekend events, transit and road closures: Nov. 15 to 17

Posted November 12, 2026 11:06 am.

It may only be November, but the Distillery District’s Winter Village will be in full swing starting this weekend and you can catch a glimpse of Santa at the Beaches Santa Claus Parade.

Keep in mind, there will also be GO transit service adjustments this weekend and the UP Express service will be replaced by buses, running between Union Station and Toronto Pearson Airport. More details can be found below.

Here’s what’s happening this weekend.

## Distillery Winter Village

The historic cobblestone streets of Distillery District will be transformed once again into the iconic Winter Village, starting this weekend and running until Jan. 3.

The tree lighting ceremony is Thursday night at 6 p.m. and special events accompanying the Winter Village kickoff featuring the festive food and drinks, local artisans, carollers and Santa and his elves that will be around for the entirety of the Christmas season.

There will also be a daily Immersive Nutcracker show that will be projected across the 360-degree floor-to-ceiling digital scape where you can get up close to the towering Nutcracker, Sugar Plum Fairy, Mouse King.

Tickets will be required for entry to the tree lighting ceremony and in the evening, but there is free entry to Distillery before 4 p.m. the whole time.

## Beaches Santa Claus Parade

Wave hello to Santa Claus in The Beaches this weekend at the annual parade. It kicks off at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Victoria Park and Kingston Road heading to Centre 55 on Main Street for a post-parade celebration.

The parade will run along Kingston Road with floats, live music and of course, Santa Claus.

## Last weekend of Royal Winter Fair

It’s your last chance to get in on the action at the Royal Winter Fair and the last day will be full of rodeo action.

There will be the Royal Rodeo Championship happening on Sunday with bull riding, saddle bronc riding, saddle bronc riding and barrel racing to cap off the 10-day Winter Fair.

You can find more details about other attractions **[on their website.](https://www.royalfair.org/)**

## Student Life Expo

Find out more about what you want to do after high school at the Student Life Expo this weekend. Representatives from universities, colleges and other organizations will be there to inform and guide students to find success after graduation.

It’s happening at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre on Nov. 15 from 12 to 5 p.m.

## Rosedale Cavalcade of Lights

Be amazed by the annual Cavalcade of Lights in Rosedale this Saturday. From 2 p.m. to 6:30 p.m., there will be festive events the whole family can enjoy topped off with the tree lighting ceremony in Scrivener Square at 5:30 p.m.

There will be a cozy Apres Ski experience, a Cavalcade Express train and get in the holiday spirit with carol singers. There will also be a little petting zoo outside of Ramsden Park.

You can find more details [on their website.](https://rosedalemainstreet.ca/event/cavalcade-of-lights-2025/)

## TTC/GO closures

**Line 2 weekend closure**

Subway service on Line 2 between Victoria Park and Kennedy stations will be replaced by shuttle buses on Saturday and Sunday for planned track work.

Regular subway service will resume on Monday at 6 a.m.

**UP Express service adjustments**

On Saturday and Sunday, there will be no UP Express train service. GO buses will run direct between Union Station Bus Terminal and Pearson Airport Terminal 1.

There will be no UP Express service at Bloor, Mount Dennis or Weston stations.

**Kitchener GO line service adjustments**

On Saturday and Sunday, GO trains will only run between Mount Pleasant and Mount Dennis GO. There will be no GO transit service at Bloor GO to Union Station.

There will be select GO buses running between Stratford or Kitchener GO and Hwy. 407 Bus Terminal.

You can find more details about alternative routes **to use here.**

**Barrie GO line service adjustments**

On Saturday, and Sunday, there will be no GO train service on the Barrie line. GO buses will run between Allandale Waterfront and Rutherford GO, then direct to Hwy. 407 Bus Terminal.

There will be no GO Transit service at Downsview Park GO.

Full details can be found **here.**

## Road Closures

**Weekend road closures**

**Beaches Santa Claus Parade**

There will be road closures in effect from 12:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. on the following streets:

- Victoria Park and Kingston Road
- Kingston Road to Main Street

**Ongoing road closures**

**Gardiner Expressway long-term closure**

As part of the **[long-term construction plan on the Gardiner Expressway](https://toronto.citynews.ca/2024/03/19/gardiner-construction-phase-two-dufferin-strachan/)**, a stretch of the westbound Gardiner has been reduced from four lanes to three. The westbound lane closure will stretch from Park Lawn Road to Grand Avenue in southern Etobicoke. The eastbound lanes along the same stretch will be narrowed, but with no lane reductions, from April 2025 to December 2026.

For full traffic and closure updates, [**click here for the latest information from 680 NewsRadio Toronto**](https://toronto.citynews.ca/traffic/).
